headline: FCC clears SpaceX to launch up to 1 million satellites
pages: The Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday gave SpaceX conditional authorization to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellites designed to work as orbital data centers. Fully built, the constellation would raise the number of satellites in orbit about 50-fold. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said the decision opens a bold new frontier for computing infrastructure. The order gives SpaceX a long runway: seven years to launch one operational satellite, until November 2035 for 100,000 operational satellites, and until November 2040 for the full constellation. Ars Technica notes the approval does not show that orbital data centers are technically or economically viable.
It is a major regulatory win for SpaceX and founder Elon Musk, who has allied himself with the Trump administration. Source: Ars Technica.
